description: Composite simulation figure from a 3D cellular-automaton (CA) model; two parts, each pairing a "Microstructure" field map (left) with a "Dislocation density" field map (right) on the YZ surface at 950 °C, every map carrying a 100 µm scale bar. (a) is a 3x2 grid for the transiently decreasing strain rate (0.1 s^-1 to 0.01 s^-1 at 0.4 strain), with rows at 0.4, 0.42 and 0.45 strain and printed DRX fractions (frist: 42.9%, 84.8%, 93.3%; total: 42.9%, 85.8%, 96.7%). Matrix grains labelled A, B and C persist as white (or red) regions. A shared colour bar "Dislocation density (x10^13 m^-2)" spans 0.01-8 with ticks 1.805, 3.666 and 5.878; printed per-row density ranges are ρ:1x10^11-3.689x10^14 m^-2, 1x10^11-1.133x10^14 m^-2 and 1x10^11-7.167x10^13 m^-2. Legend: "White grains: matrix, Green grains: first stage, Red grains: second stage". (b) is the constant 0.01 s^-1 case at 0.42 strain, DRX fraction 83.0%, with a many-coloured microstructure and a dislocation-density map of ρ = 1x10^11-5.169x10^13 m^-2. Despite comparable DRX fractions, the transient case keeps much higher dislocation density in matrix grains A, B, C, which the figure uses to explain continued DRX-grain growth.

subfigures.description: A 3-row x 2-column set of simulated YZ-surface field maps at 950 °C for the transiently decreasing strain rate (0.1 s^-1 to 0.01 s^-1 at 0.4 strain). Left column 'Microstructure' (white = matrix grains A, B, C; green = first-stage DRX grains; red = second-stage DRX grains), right column 'Dislocation density' on a shared colour bar in x10^13 m^-2. Rows are 0.4 strain (DRX fraction frist 42.9%, total 42.9%), 0.42 strain (frist 84.8%, total 85.8%) and 0.45 strain (frist 93.3%, total 96.7%); each map has a 100 µm scale bar.

Constant strain rate 0.01 s^-1 at 0.42 strain: a multi-coloured microstructure map (each grain a different colour, no printed colour key) beside a 'Dislocation density' map with ρ:1x10^11-5.169x10^13 m^-2, both with 100 µm scale bars. Printed DRX fraction: 83.0%. The dislocation-density field is broadly uniform blue/green with only thin high-density boundaries, unlike the hot matrix regions of (a).

observations.observation: The shared colour bar on the right of (a) is labelled 'Dislocation density (x10^13 m^-2)' with printed ticks 8, 5.878, 3.666, 1.805 and 0.01.
In (a) the 0.4 strain row prints 'DRX fraction(frist: 42.9%; total: 42.9%)' and a dislocation-density range 'ρ:1x10^11-3.689x10^14 m^-2'.
In (a) the 0.42 strain row prints 'DRX fraction(frist: 84.8%; total: 85.8%)' and 'ρ:1x10^11-1.133x10^14 m^-2'.
In (a) the 0.45 strain row prints 'DRX fraction(frist: 93.3%; total: 96.7%)' and 'ρ:1x10^11-7.167x10^13 m^-2'.
In (b) the printed DRX fraction is 83.0% at 0.42 strain and the dislocation-density range is 'ρ:1x10^11-5.169x10^13 m^-2'.
A legend beneath the (a) microstructures reads 'White grains: matrix', 'Green grains: first stage' and 'Red grains: second stage'.
Every one of the eight field maps carries a 100 µm scale bar, so all maps are at the same length scale.
Red (second-stage) grains are essentially absent in the 0.4 and 0.42 strain microstructure maps of (a) and appear only in the 0.45 strain map.

In the 0.42 and 0.45 strain dislocation-density maps of (a), the regions marked A, B and C appear warm (orange/red on the colour bar) while surrounding recrystallised grains are blue/green, i.e. the matrix retains visibly higher dislocation density.
The (b) microstructure uses many distinct grain colours rather than the three-colour matrix/first-stage/second-stage scheme of (a), and no colour key for it is printed in the figure.

The caption states the figure shows simulated evolutions of microstructure and dislocation density distribution on the YZ surface under transiently decreasing and constant strain rates at 950 °C: (a) transient decrease from 0.1 s^-1 to 0.01 s^-1 at 0.4 strain, (b) constant 0.01 s^-1 at 0.42 strain.

The citing text states that after the strain rate suddenly decreased, the dislocation density of matrix grains including A, B and C remained much higher than under a constant 0.01 s^-1 at 0.42 strain, so the first-stage DRX grains underwent further growth, giving a higher DRX fraction.

The citing text states that although the total recrystallisation fraction in (a) was close to that at the constant 0.01 s^-1 condition in (b), the two dislocation-density distributions were evidently different.
